transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

It is very likely not faulty at all. On Beko induction hobs, a flashing 'U' (or a pan symbol) typically means the hob cannot detect suitable cookware on that zone. Induction zones only heat magnetic pans of the right size; if the base is non-magnetic (like some aluminium or copper), warped, or too small, it will flash 'U'. Please try placing a saucepan you know works on another induction hob on this one. If it heats up normally, your original pan was simply not compatible with induction. If it still flashes 'U' even with a known-compatible pan, then there may be an installation or hardware fault to investigate.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I tried my cast-iron casserole on the same zone and that heated up fine! It's only my aluminium saucepans and a copper-bottomed pan that flash the U. So is it the pans?

Yes, it is most likely the pans. Induction hobs only work with magnetic cookware; aluminium and copper are non-magnetic, so the hob correctly refuses to heat them. Your cast-iron casserole worked because iron is magnetic. This suggests your new Beko hob is functioning perfectly and is not faulty at all.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
